thesis: Wynn Resorts is a developer and operator of luxury integrated casino resorts. **[Fact]** Through roughly **72%** ownership of Wynn Macau, Limited, the company runs Wynn Palace and Wynn Macau in Macau. **[Fact]** In the U.S., it owns and operates Wynn Las Vegas and Encore on the Strip and Encore Boston Harbor in Massachusetts. **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated operating revenues were **$7.14 billion** (up **0.1%** year over year). **[Fact]** The company also holds a **40%** equity interest in a joint venture building Wynn Al Marjan Island in the United Arab Emirates, targeted to open in **2027**. **[Inference]** Owner economics are driven by gaming win (especially VIP and premium mass in Macau), hotel occupancy and average daily rate, food and beverage spend, and capital spending to maintain ultra-luxury positioning.
why_market_wrong: There is **no classic dated mispricing signal** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** Generalists often bucket Wynn with highly levered U.S. regional casinos, while filings show a bifurcated portfolio: recovering Macau VIP and mass win (Q1 2026 Macau revenue **+14.2%** year over year) and a stable Las Vegas premium franchise. **[Fact]** FY2025 net income attributable to Wynn Resorts fell **35%** to **$327 million** even though operating revenues were flat, driven by higher income taxes (**+$101 million**) and lower interest income, not operating collapse. **[Inference]** Bears may overweight **$10.5 billion** of long-term debt and thin parent equity (**$275 million**) and underweight **$1.35 billion** of operating cash flow and **$2.22 billion** of Adjusted Property EBITDAR. **[Inference]** Bulls may extrapolate Q1 2026 momentum without modeling **~$660 million** of annual capital spending and UAE pre-opening cash needs.
